subject: Very Large Datasets, Importing, And Multiple crosses

messages.author: e397edc35215e780
messages.subject: Very Large Datasets, Importing, And Multiple crosses
parts:
Hi!
I hope it's not against the rules to ask two questions in one post!

  1. The first question that I have is how to structure a very large data set for use in r/qtl. I've got RAD data with so many loci that I can't edit the data in Excel. This has presented a problem because, despite my best efforts, r/qtl doesn't want to recognize my "chromosome" line when there are two fields with "NA" in them. When I've tried with a smaller data set in excel, deleting "NA" and saving it as a csv works just fine. The process that I'm using to create the read.cross data set is by assembling it from a .vcf output. This is in the format ".012", which means that I get two files that I'm combining: 1) a file with all of the loci and the number of "reference alleles" at each (0 = BB, 1 = BA, 2 = AA) 2) a file with all of the individual identifiers. I'm gluing these files together in R, but to insert the line that has "chromosome number" on it (I'm calling them all chromosome 1 since I don't have that information yet), I have to create a list that contains the blank cells, as described in the tutorial.

    I've used this code to do this:
    > chromosome <- c(NA,NA,rep(1,43975)) where 43975 is the number of loci

    Then glue this to the top, producing the attached file. When I run read.cross, I get the following error:
    > sample_cross <- read.cross(file = "small_matrix.csv", format = 'csv', na.strings = c("-1", "NA"),  genotypes = c("0", "1", "2"), alleles = c("A", "B"))

    Error in read.cross.csv(dir, file, na.strings, genotypes, estimate.map,  :
    You must include at least one phenotype (e.g., an index). There was this value in the first column of the second row 'NA' where was supposed to be nothing.


  2. My second question is about study design. My data (155 individuals) are spread across a number of crosses, some backcross and some intercross. I'm thinking that I should be analyzing them separately (at least by type, but they have different parents, so maybe also by brood?), but I haven't seen much in the literature on what to do with multiple families. Any suggestions, or could you point me towards resources for this problem? To be clear, I'm working with only one phenotype, but multiple lines of crosses from (non-model system) wild-caught individuals.
Thank you so much for your time, and for the software!

Best,
Evan

You need to get rid of the "NA"s in those initial cells; the initial cells in the 2nd and third rows need to be completely empty.

R/qtl has limited ability for the joint analysis of multiple crosses. But if you have just 155 individuals total, I'd definitely look for ways to synthesize the data, since any one cross would not be very informative for QTL analysis.

karl
